chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought an atheist (Zindiq), so he struck his neck.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a Zindiq according to the narration of Amir al-Mu'minin?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the precedent for executing the *Zindiq* (heretic) by striking the neck, a method distinct from the standard sword execution for male apostates in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the early Caliphate's approach to dealing with doctrinal deviants, linking the physical penalty to the preservation of religious orthodoxy. The narration underscores the authority of the Imam in determining the specific mode of execution based on the nature of the heresy.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asamma, from Misma’a,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that they came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> with an atheist, so he<sup>asws</sup> struck his neck’.
